They nailed up these spoils to the gods in the halls throughout Greece, an ancient delight.
this is the brightness of an old vine
rejoicing no less than in Zeus-sent brightness (thus Porson for διόσ-νότῳ γᾶν εἰ) the sowing
I rejoice in these things being accomplished favorably for my land.
the same as δάπεδον [ground], soil, earth

where M has δάπεδα [grounds] with the meter corrupted: for δάπεδον [ground] is said with the first syllable short. By the same error in Lycophron 617 τοῦ τειχοποιοῦ γαπέδων Ἀμοιβέως [of the wall-building grounds of Amoebeus] not a few manuscripts have δαπέδων [grounds]. Therefore Porson rightly restored γάπεδα [grounds] to Aeschylus in his note on Euripides' Orestes v. 324, a form which the tragedians sometimes used where δάπεδον [ground] would not fit the meter, preserving the Doric alpha, as they did in γάμορος γάϊος γαπόνος γάποτος γατόμος δάϊος νάϊος [landowner, of the earth, farmer, earth-drunk, earth-cutting, hostile, of a temple] and other words, about which the testimony of Stephanus of Byzantium is explicit under the entry Γῆ: λέγεται καὶ γήπεδον (τὸ πρὸς τοῖς οἴκοις ἐν πόλει κηπίον), ὅπερ οἱ τραγικοὶ διὰ τοῦ ἃ φασὶ δωρίζοντες [it is also called γήπεδον (the garden by the houses in the city), which the tragedians say with alpha, Doricizing]. Where what he says about the meaning of the word must be cautioned not to refer to the tragedians, whom it is not likely ever spoke about little gardens situated before houses. They undoubtedly said γάπεδον [ground] never otherwise than to mean γῆς πέδον [plain of earth]. The most ancient examples of the other meaning are found in Plato and Aristotle, such as Phrynichus had in mind when he said about the use of the word what is read in Bekker's Anecdota p. 32, 1, also appended by Stephanus of Byzantium, although omitting Phrynichus' name, after the words cited by me above. The gloss of Hesychius γάπεδα: ἀγροικικαὶ οἰκίαι [grounds: rustic dwellings] although it could be taken from some Doric prose writer, nevertheless seems more probably to refer to the tragedians, with an interpretation attached that is foreign to the usage of the tragedians.
